$comment: Authored from docs/plan/state-machines/offer-negotiation.md. The invariants below are the ones spike S-10 measured under 750 concurrent acceptances: zero double acceptances, zero deadlocks.
subject: public.offers.status

states.name: pending
states.meaning: Live, within TTL, awaiting the counterparty

states.name: countered
states.meaning: Superseded by a counter-offer in the same thread

states.name: accepted
states.meaning: Won the request. Exactly one per request, ever

states.name: withdrawn
states.meaning: Pulled by its author before acceptance

states.name: expired
states.meaning: TTL elapsed, or a sibling offer was accepted

transitions.guard: Provider eligible; request published, offers_received or negotiating; not self-dealing; amount within the country's guardrails; no unresolved blocking job
Round count below the max (default 5); the author is the counterparty, not the same side twice
effects: a new pending offer in the thread

transitions.guard: Offer pending and unexpired; provider still eligible; request in an acceptable state
effects: all sibling offers to expired in the same transaction
notify the customer if it was the last active offer
if no pending offers remain, request back to published
emitted as part of the accept transaction, never separately

transitions.guard: Provider became ineligible: suspended, documents expired, or offline past the grace period
effects: notify the provider with the reason

invariants: At most one accepted offer per request, ever. Enforced by locking the request row, not by a unique index alone: the index would reject the second write, but the lock lets the server return a meaningful error instead of a constraint violation.
Accepting expires siblings in the same transaction. A provider must never see an offer as live after losing it.
Exactly one offer-accepted event. The outbox drives payment, notifications and analytics, and a double fire would double-charge.
A replayed accept with the same idempotency key returns the original outcome and does not act again.
A losing caller gets a stable code, never a raw exception: ERR_OFFER_NOT_ACTIVE, ERR_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION or ERR_OFFER_EXPIRED.

competitive_invariant.rule: A provider never reads another provider's offer amount.
enforced_at: RLS: offers_read limits a provider to their own thread
Realtime: the offer broadcast goes to request:{id}:customer and to request:{id}:provider:{provider_id}, never to a shared request topic
competitive_invariant.note: Neither layer relies on the client choosing not to render something.
